text.text_excerpt: For one, the location this CVS has cannot be beat. One block away from Bourbon and extra bonus that they do not over charge on things. There is also a Walgreens down the block and a Brother's a block around the corner if you can't find what you are looking for here. There are 2 staffed checkout counters and 4 self-checkout stations. On busier days, the line will sometimes drag into the wine aisles, but in general, things move along pretty quick. The pharmacy techs are some of the nicest people ever :) The other staff range anywhere from moderately helpful to grumpy, but hey, it's really not their fault. I'm sure they have seen enough of the Canal-Bourbon Street crowd to last them a lifeti...

Need to pick up something before you head onto Bourbon Street and find that the Walgreens at the corner is closed? Or maybe you need to detox after all the fun and every other place just sells more junk food and booze? Have no fear, CVS is here! When I was in New Orleans with a new friend I made, we were looking for some OJ. Yes, orange juice at night. We just went through the French Quarter and were looking to quench our thirst. Unfortunately, Walgreens wasn't an option for us, but luckily CVS was open! It's 24 hours and has everything you might need before/after your excursions into the Crescent City. We picked up some OJ and a power bar and we were off. This CVS is definitely a go. It ...

In the words of my high school self, "gosh this places was hella convenient". I am just elated with the number of convenience stores in the New Orleans (downtown & French Quarter area). Seriously though, I just wish there were some closer to other parts, too. They always come to my rescue here. Each time I have walked into a CVS in NOLA, I have found exactly what I needed, ummmmm, pretty much immediately. The aisles are so well let and so organized that it takes me no time at all to find exactly what I need. Need chips, dairy, cosmetics and medication, they've got them!
